title: oscore_protect_response payload-bounds underflow: pt_len == sizeof(plaintext) makes 'sizeof - pt_len - 1' wrap to SIZE_MAX
description: Found by worker2 security review pass of project-LICHEN-worker6-nugy (Kimi K3, 2026-09-09). oscore_protect.c:632-638: the options-capacity check at line 624 rejects only options_len > CONFIG_LICHEN_OSCORE_PLAINTEXT_MAX - 1, so options_len == MAX-1 passes and pt_len becomes exactly sizeof(plaintext). The payload guard then computes sizeof(plaintext) - pt_len - 1 which underflows to SIZE_MAX, so the check never fires for payload_len > 0; line 637 (plaintext[pt_len++] = 0xFF) writes one byte past the stack buffer and line 638's memcpy writes payload_len bytes out of bounds. The sibling oscore_protect_request guards exactly this with an explicit pt_len == sizeof(plaintext) test (oscore_protect.c:167); protect_response lacks it. Suggested fix (mirror the request-side guard): if (payload_len > 0) { if (pt_len == sizeof(plaintext) || payload_len > sizeof(plaintext) - pt_len - 1) { ret = OSCORE_ERR_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL; goto cleanup; } }. Not radio-reachable today: all in-tree callers pass <=3 option bytes (nugy's new CF forwarding) and server-side payload sizes; latent memory-safety on the public options data path only. OScore internals have a human-only edit bar (AGENTS.md) - leaving for Mark.
